I added an `ENISOWeekDateParser` to the English parsers and it works in both `chrono.strict` and `chrono.casual`. The whole test suite passes with `npx jest` (159 suites, 786 tests). The type check passes and Prettier reports the files as already formatted. I haven't committed anything.

**The parser** (`src/locales/en/parsers/ENISOWeekDateParser.ts`)
- It reads `YYYY-Www`, `YYYY-Www-D`, `YYYYWww` and `YYYYWwwD`, with `W` in either case. With no weekday digit it gives the Monday of that week.
- Year, month, day and weekday are assigned as certain; the time is left implied, and the result carries the tag `parser/ENISOWeekDateParser`.
- The weekday is stored in chrono's own numbering (0 = Sunday), so an ISO 7 becomes 0.
- The year stored is the calendar year of the date, which can differ from the week-year: `2020-W01-1` is 30 Dec 2019, and `2015-W53-5` is 1 Jan 2016.
- Week 00, weeks above 53, and week 53 in a year that has only 52 weeks all give no result.
- **Bad weekday digit:** a 0, 8 or 9 in the weekday position also gives no result, and the parser doesn't fall back to a shorter match. For example, `2020-W10-8` returns nothing rather than `2020-W10`.

**Registration:** I added it to the parser list in `src/locales/en/configuration.ts`. Strict mode, casual mode and the GB variant all build from that list, so all three get it.

**Tests** (`test/en/en_iso_week_date.test.ts`): 33 cases, each in its own `test(...)` block with a fixed reference date, following `AGENTS.md`. They cover all four forms, lowercase `w`, Sunday, week dates inside a sentence (checking index and text), dates that fall in the previous or next calendar year, valid and invalid week 53, strict and casual modes, and every rejection case.

I also checked the date arithmetic against an independent calculation for every day from 1900 to 2100 and for every year's week 53. Everything matched, and I deleted that temporary test afterwards.

**Decision for you:** I made the parser reject a few more cases than you listed, all following the "not even a shorter one" rule:
- A compact week followed by a hyphenated digit, like `2020W10-3`, is rejected.
- Extra digits after the weekday, like `2020-W10-89`, are rejected.
- A week date run directly into a hyphen and another number, like `2020-W01-2020-W05`, is rejected. If you want that form to work, write it with spaces or the ISO `/` separator (`2020-W01/2020-W05`), which do.

None of these has a dedicated test. If you'd rather allow any of them, it's a one-line change to the regex.

I added ISO 8601 week date support to the English parsers. The full suite passes (159 suites, 772 tests, including the 19 new ones), the type check is clean, and prettier made no changes. I haven't committed anything.

**What changed**
- **`src/locales/en/parsers/ENISOWeekDateParser.ts`** (new): extends `AbstractParserWithWordBoundaryChecking` and handles `YYYY-Www`, `YYYY-Www-D`, `YYYYWww` and `YYYYWwwD`, with `W` in either case. A week without a weekday digit gives that week's Monday. Year, month, day and weekday are assigned and the time is left implied (noon by default). Results carry the tag `parser/ENISOWeekDateParser`.
- **`src/locales/en/configuration.ts`**: the parser is registered in `createConfiguration`, so `chrono.strict`, `chrono.casual` and `chrono.GB` all use it.
- **`test/en/en_iso_week_date.test.ts`** (new): each case is a separate `test(...)` with a fixed reference date. It covers all four forms, lowercase `w`, Sunday (`7` gives weekday `0`), week 1 starting in the previous calendar year, week 53 in 2020 and 2026, a match inside a sentence (index and text checked), strict mode, and a week date followed by a time (`2020-W10-5 at 10am` merges into a single date and time). The negative cases are week 00, week 54, week 53 of 2021, weekday 0, 8 and 9, and a mixed form.

**How invalid input is rejected**
- The pattern captures any weekday digit and any week number, and the code then checks their ranges. So `2020-W01-8` gives no result at all, rather than falling back to `2020-W01`.
- The pattern also refuses to stop early when a digit follows, so `2020-W01-89` and `2020W0112` produce nothing.
- Week 53 is accepted only when the year starts or ends on a Thursday.

**One choice beyond your spec:** a week date that mixes the two forms, like `2020-W013` or `2020W01-3`, is rejected entirely. ISO doesn't allow that mix and it isn't one of your four forms; if you'd rather accept it, it's a one-line change.

**Extra check:** before writing the tests, I ran a temporary script (now deleted) that compared the parser with a separate ISO-week calculation for sampled dates from 1900 to 2100, and checked week 53 for every year. There were no mismatches.

**Known limitations**
- A combined week date and time like `2020-W01-1T10:00` isn't recognised as a week date. It was out of scope.
- Years 0000–0099 get the right year, month and day values, but chrono's own date conversion doesn't handle such early years.

I added `ENISOWeekDateParser` and registered it for both `chrono.strict` and `chrono.casual`. The full suite passes (`npx jest`: 159 suites, 764 tests), including the 11 new tests, and `tsc --noEmit` is clean. Nothing is committed.

**What changed**
- **`src/locales/en/parsers/ENISOWeekDateParser.ts`**:
  - Recognizes `YYYY-Www`, `YYYY-Www-D`, `YYYYWww` and `YYYYWwwD`, with `W` in either case.
  - Without a weekday digit it gives the Monday of that week.
  - The result's text is exactly the week date. Year, month, day and weekday are assigned and the time is implied. It carries the tag `parser/ENISOWeekDateParser`.
  - Weekday 7 (Sunday) becomes chrono's weekday `0`.
  - The ISO year can differ from the calendar year: `2020-W01-1` gives Dec 30, 2019, and `2015-W53-7` gives Jan 3, 2016.
- **`src/locales/en/configuration.ts`**: added the parser to the shared parser list, so both configurations use it.
- **`test/en/en_iso_week_date.test.ts`**: one explicit `testSingleCase` / `testUnexpectedResult` call per case with a fixed reference date, following the AGENTS.md conventions.

**What gets no result at all**
- Week 00, weeks above 53, and week 53 in a year with only 52 weeks (e.g. `2021-W53`, `2019W53`).
- Weekday digits 0, 8 or 9 (e.g. `2020-W10-8`, `2020W108`). These don't fall back to the shorter `2020-W10` either.
- Extra digits after the weekday (`2020-W10-12`, `2020W1012`) and a one-digit week (`2020-W1`).

**Decision for you:** mixing the two styles, as in `2020W10-1` or `2020-W101`, isn't one of the four forms, so I reject it entirely. The alternative would have been to accept the shorter `2020W10`, but that conflicts with the "not even a shorter one" rule. It's a one-line check in `innerExtract` if you'd rather be lenient.

Because the time is left implied, a following time merges in the usual way: `2020-W10-2 at 10am` parses as Mar 3, 2020, 10:00. Before this change, nothing in the English parsers matched any of these inputs, so no existing results change.
